subject: Post-incident data chain clearance and verification
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Mathews <sarah.mathews@aurorabk.com>, security@aurorabk.com
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident data chain clearance and verification

Sarah / Aurora security team —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As promised, we've completed a targeted verification of the artifacts relevant to the event on 2026-10-30 and are sharing the reconciliation materials for your audit team to review. Summary of what we ran and attached: 

- audit_manifest_20261101.csv — inventory of artifacts we sampled (tokenized request ids, pipeline batch ids, retention buckets)
- log_hashes_20261101.txt — SHA256 hashes for each rotated log file and the archive slices we pulled for review
- redwood_postmortem_summary.pdf — short write-up of timeline, root cause, and mitigations (high-level)

What we validated:
- No customer payloads were present in the rotated runtime debug traces we sampled (sampling windows noted in the manifest).
- Hash reconciliation shows matched checksums at each hop (service -> storage -> archive) for the sampled set; no mismatches detected.
- No S3 object ACL changes were performed during the incident window; access logs show only internal service principals and our infra scanner.

Request: can your audit team confirm receipt and advise if they need additional ranges (we can expand sampling to cover the full 48h window around the incident). We can also provide an export of the signed hash manifest if you'd like a copy to ingest into your records.

Next steps (from our side): Mina will attach the verification command logs and the ephemeral keys rotated post-incident; Marissa will prepare a brief clearance note for your compliance team once you confirm you have everything you need.

Appreciate the quick coordination — please loop in your auditor alias if you want us to push the S3 object manifest to a secure transfer.

—
Karthik Iyer
Head of Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Mathews <sarah.mathews@aurorabk.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, security@aurorabk.com
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident data chain clearance and verification

Karthik —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. I downloaded the manifest and hash list and will pass them to our external auditors. A couple of quick clarifications from my side: 

1) When you say "sampling windows" in the manifest, does that mean you sampled a subset of rotated logs or every rotated file from the affected hosts? Would prefer full-file checks for any rotated object that overlaps 2026-10-30 02:00-06:00 UTC.

2) Can you confirm whether any debug-level traces were enabled transiently during the incident? We noted an increase in verbose logs on our end and want to be sure there wasn't any client-side payload persisted.

3) Please provide the signed manifest option if available — we'll ingest that into our chain-of-custody registry. 

If possible, could you also post the audit materials to the secure transfer URL we provided earlier (devops+audits@aurorabk.com).

Thanks —
Sarah
Director, Security Operations
AuroraBank

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Mathews <sarah.mathews@aurorabk.com>, security@aurorabk.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident data chain clearance and verification — verification details

Sarah / team —

Following up with technical specifics you asked for. Apologies for the longer note — want to make the verification transparent for your auditors. Short answers first: we sampled rotated files (every rotated file) for hosts that produced logs during the 2026-10-30 incident window; we then expanded to a random 10% of archive slices for full-file verification per your 02:00-06:00 UTC range. No debug traces were persisted to object storage.

Process we executed (high level):
1) Identified host IDs by correlating request ids from ingress traces to runtime logs (pipeline tag: run-20261030*).
2) Exported rotated log objects to temporary audit bucket (read-only) and computed SHA256 checksums with our in-house verifier (script: tools/audit/hash_check_v2.sh).
3) Recomputed checksums for archive slices (compressed) and compared to rotated file hashes; mismatches flagged zero.
4) Cross-checked S3 server access logs for GetObject/PutObject events in the 2026-10-30 00:00-12:00 UTC window and validated principal identities.
5) Generated a signed manifest (PKCS7) using our signing key (fingerprint: AB:3F:9D:... truncated) and included the .sig in the manifest bundle; attached a copy to the secure transfer if you need it.

Items we included with this message (pushed to devops+audits@aurorabk.com per your request):
- audit_manifest_20261101.csv (full sample list; includes object keys and timestamps)
- log_hashes_20261101.txt (SHA256 lines: <object-key> <sha256>)
- verifier_command_log_20261101.txt (CLI commands and checksums we executed)
- signed_manifest_20261101.sig (PKCS7)

Notes/observations:
- The only non-standard artifact we found was a transient debug trace that was present in ephemeral memory but never flushed to disk/storage; trace IDs are in the manifest for completeness.
- We rotated the ephemeral signing key for the manifest immediately after generation and recorded rotation in the postmortem.

If your auditors want, we can run the same verification against the full set (not just rotated files) but that will add ≈3–4 hours to the work and we can schedule it tomorrow.

Thanks —
Mina Haddad
SR. Security Engineer, Incident Response
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Mathews <sarah.mathews@aurorabk.com>, devops+audits@aurorabk.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T15:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident data chain clearance and verification — clearance memo

Sarah / Aurora team —

Following Mina's technical note and the artifacts you've received, this is Redwood's formal clearance memo for your records: 

- Scope: verification covers rotated runtime logs and archived slices for hosts that were active during the 2026-10-30 incident window (we expanded to full-file checks for 02:00-06:00 UTC at your request).
- Outcome: No customer payloads were found in stored artifacts. Hash reconciliation across each step (service -> object store -> archive) shows no integrity failures for the verified set.
- Chain-of-custody: signed_manifest_20261101.sig accompanies the CSV manifest and has been uploaded to the secure transfer endpoint you provided; signature fingerprint (PKCS7): AB:3F:9D:...
- Actions taken: ephemeral keys rotated; verifier logs retained in a read-only audit bucket; we've attached the incident ticket for cross-reference: INC-20261.

Attachments: audit_manifest_20261101.csv (inventory), log_hashes_20261101.txt (checksums), redwood_postmortem_summary.pdf (high-level timeline and mitigations). Please confirm you have everything you need or if your compliance team requires a notarized copy of the manifest.

If Aurora considers this sufficient to close the matter on your side, reply here with confirmation and we'll update the customer-facing incident record and close the audit subtask.

Thanks for the partnership on this — we know these processes are stressful and appreciate the clear requests that made the verification quicker.

—
Marissa Cole
Principal, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
